title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standardized on-call and incident response process, runbook templates, postmortem guidance, rotation and escalation policies, game day guidance, and status page / customer communications templates. It is the canonical reference for incident management across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to all services that affect customer-facing inference (API gateway, model-serving runtime, scheduler, GPU fleet, billing/quotas, and observability pipelines).
- Excludes: non-production sandbox environments (see separate sandbox runbooks).

Goals:
- Restore customer-impacting service quickly and safely.
- Provide clear stakeholder communications during incidents.
- Capture root cause and actions to prevent recurrence.
- Ensure predictable on-call rotations and escalation.

Key Roles and Responsibilities:
- Primary On-call (Pager): first responder for pages and initial triage.
- Secondary On-call: backs up Primary if escalation is needed or primary is overloaded.
- Incident Commander (IC): owns incident coordination, timeline, and final decisions.
- Communication Lead: drafts public/internal updates and coordinates with Customer Success.
- Engineering Owner: team responsible for triage and mitigation for the affected service.
- SRE Lead: provides operational guidance and authorizes mitigations that affect infrastructure.
- Exec Pager: notified for Sev 0 incidents after initial mitigation if impact is widespread.

Severity Definitions and Target Objectives:
- Sev 0 (P0): Complete service outage with major customer impact (many customers affected, API unavailable). Response: page immediately, acknowledge within 5 minutes. Target time-to-mitigate (initial workaround): 30 minutes.
- Sev 1 (P1): Significant degradation or large subset of customers affected. Acknowledge within 15 minutes. Target mitigation (workaround): 2 hours.
- Sev 2 (P2): Partial degradation, small set of customers impacted, or elevated error rates. Acknowledge within 1 hour. Target mitigation: same business day.
- Sev 3 (P3): Informational or low-impact issues, no customer-facing degradation. Track in issue tracker.

SLOs and Alerting Thresholds (examples):
- API 5xx rate: alert when 5xx rate > 2% for 3m (P1).
- Median latency (95th percentile): alert when p95 > 500ms for 5m (P1).
- GPU node health: alert when node drain rate > 10% of pool (P1).
- Telemetry ingestion lag: alert when > 5 minutes sustained (P2).

Incident Lifecycle (step-by-step):
1) Detection
  - Alerts / PagerDuty / customer reports / status page indicators.
  - Primary on-call acknowledges page and posts an initial incident stub in the incident tracker (Confluence incident page template).
2) Triage
  - Primary collects basic facts: time, manifesting symptom, impact, services affected, recent deploys.
  - Determine severity using definitions above.
  - Assign Incident Commander if severity >= P1.
3) Mitigation
  - IC coordinates triage, requests resources (secondary, engineering on-call), and authorizes mitigations.
  - Prioritize customer-visible workarounds before permanent fixes.
4) Communication
  - Communication lead posts initial status on internal Slack #incidents and public status page. Use templates below.
  - Provide updates every 15-30 minutes for P0, every 30-60 minutes for P1 until mitigated.
5) Recovery & Verify
  - Confirm metrics and customer-reported experiences are back to baseline.
  - Maintain watch until stable and hand back to standard on-call rotation.
6) Postmortem
  - Owner completes a postmortem within 72 hours for P0/P1 and within 7 days for P2. Postmortem must include timeline, impact, root cause, remediation plan, action owners, and verification criteria.

Runbook Template (required fields):
- Title: short service name and primary symptom.
- Pager escalation: Primary -> Secondary -> IC -> Engineering lead -> Exec.
- Initial checks (commands & dashboards):
  1. Check API gateway health: curl -I https://api.redwood.example/health || check gateway dashboard (Grafana: API-GW / Health).
  2. Check model-serving pods: kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=model-serving && kubectl describe pod <pod> for recent OOMs or restarts.
  3. Check GPU node status: kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true && nohup nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY on node (SSH) or use fleet dashboard.
  4. Observe KV cache misses/hit ratio in metrics (Metric: serving.kv_cache.hit_ratio).
  5. Check message queue/backlog: queue consumer lag > 100k -> possible processing outage.
- Quick mitigations (ordered):
  1. Restart a failing pod: kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serving -n runtime (only if safe).
  2. Scale up replicas temporarily: kubectl scale deployment/model-serving --replicas=<$n> -n runtime.
  3. Re-route traffic to fallback model variant via router API: POST /admin/route-fallback {service: "model-serving", variant: "fast-quant"}.
  4. Fallback to regional capacity: modify routing policy in the control plane.
- When to escalate: any data loss, persistent 5xx for > 5m, or mitigation requires schema change.
- Post-incident actions: collect logs, upload core dumps to S3, tag incident in issue tracker.

Example Runbook: GPU Driver OOM
- Symptom: GPU pods failing with CUDA OOM on high concurrency.
- Initial checks: check dmesg on node, confirm driver version mismatch, check pod resource requests.
- Quick mitigations: reduce per-pod concurrency, evict large-batch jobs, roll out quantized model variant, cordon & reboot node if driver state corrupted.
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime team on-call.

On-call Rotation Policy:
- Rotation length: 2-week primary rotations with 1-week secondary overlaps (Primary rotates every 2 weeks; Secondary rotates offset by 1 week).
- Handoff checklist (start of shift): review open incidents, check personal access to pager and runbook list, verify contact info up-to-date in PagerDuty.
- Handoff checklist (end of shift): update incident pages, confirm no outstanding P1/P0, transfer temporary tokens/credentials.
- Maximum weekly pages threshold: if an on-call receives > 20 pages in a week, the SRE lead will review workload and consider rotation adjustment.
- Escalation: if Primary does not acknowledge within defined threshold (5m for P0, 15m for P1), Secondary is automatically paged by PagerDuty escalation policy.

Game Day Program:
- Frequency: quarterly company-wide game days and monthly team-level drills.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test cross-team coordination, exercise status page and comms cadence, validate failover to Dedicated/Regional capacity.
- Typical scenarios: API gateway outage, GPU fleet degraded, large-scale KV cache invalidation, telemetry blackout.
- After-action: do a short retro 24-48 hours after game day and produce a prioritized action list with owners and due dates.

Postmortem Requirements and Template (mandatory for P0/P1):
- Title
- Summary (one-paragraph)
- Impact (customers affected, duration, revenue/SLAs impacted)
- Timeline (ordered timestamps, actor, action)
- Root cause analysis (why it happened)
- Contributing factors
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and target due dates
- Verification plan (how we will validate the fix)
- Blameless language and distribution list

Example Postmortem Action Items:
- Patch driver version validation to CI (owner: infra-team, due: 2026-03-01).
- Add alert for KV cache miss spike (owner: observability, due: 2026-02-20).
- Create a runbook for rolling rollback of model variants (owner: eng-serving-runtime, due: 2026-03-10).

Status Page and Customer Communications Templates:
- Status page initial entry (short):
  Title: API Latency / 5xx spike
  Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency and 5xx errors for text generation.
  Current status: Investigating.
  Updated at: <UTC timestamp>
- Public update cadence: Every 30 minutes for Sev 0 until mitigation, then every 2 hours until resolved.
- Customer communication (initial):
  Subject: Incident: Increased latency and errors for Redwood API
  Body: "We are investigating reports of increased latency and elevated error rates affecting text generation requests. Our on-call team is actively triaging. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. If you are experiencing urgent production impact, please contact your Customer Success rep or reply to this message."
- Internal update (Slack):
  - Short headline, what we know, what we're doing, next update ETA, owners. Example:
  "[P0] API 5xx spike — Investigating. Affected: Hosted API (all regions). Initial mitigation: routing to regional fallback in progress. IC: Asha Patel. Comm lead: Maya Chen. Next update in 15m."

Communication Best Practices:
- Use plain, non-technical language for public updates; more detail for paying customers via private comms.
- Avoid speculation: only state verified facts.
- Timestamp every update and attach metric/screenshot links when available.
- Provide next steps and expected ETA for remediation when possible.

Tooling and Artifacts:
- Pager: PagerDuty (primary). Escalation policies configured per severity.
- Incident tracker: Confluence incident template + JIRA ticket for long-term work.
- Metrics and dashboards: Grafana (dashboards: API-GW, Serving-Runtime, GPU-Fleet).
- Log store: Loki (service logs), Elastic (search), S3 for archived core dumps.
- Status page: status.redwood.example (public) and private status for enterprise customers.

Training and Onboarding:
- New on-call engineers must complete a 1-week onboarding that includes runbook review, shadowing, and a mini game day.
- Maintain a public runbook index (Confluence) with owners and last-tested date.

Retention and Review:
- Runbooks must be reviewed at least quarterly; owners will receive automated review reminders.
- Postmortems for P0/P1 will be reviewed in Monthly Reliability Review meeting.
- Action item follow-ups tracked in JIRA and must include verification criteria.

Appendices:
- Quick commands cheat sheet
  - Check pods: kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide
  - Restart deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> -n <ns>
  - Check node GPU: ssh gpu-node-<id> dmesg | tail -n 200
  - Re-route traffic: curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.example/route -d '{"service":"model-serving","variant":"fallback"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

- Contact matrix (example):
  - Primary on-call: see PagerDuty schedule (team: eng-serving-runtime)
  - Secondary on-call: see PagerDuty schedule (team: eng-serving-runtime)
  - SRE lead: Liam O'Connor
  - Customer Success on-call: Diego Alvarez

Document maintenance:
- Author: Asha Patel (eng-sre)
- Last updated: 2026-02-10
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev 0/P1 incident.

Related documents:
- SLO and error budget policy: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Capacity playbook: /confluence/eng-infra/capacity-planning

Feedback and improvements:
- Send corrections or suggestions to #incidents-feedback in Slack or create a PR against this page in Confluence.
